reasoning_checks: Cost object/traceability and activity-based cost behavior are separate classifications. Fixed versus variable is not equated with unavoidable versus avoidable; sunk expenditure is distinct from relevant future resale or alternative-use value.

Contribution includes all supplied variable costs. One-product break-even and target-profit formulas are derived, with zero/negative contribution, zero fixed cost, integer quantities and infeasible thresholds addressed. Multi-product break-even explicitly freezes a unit mix and distinguishes revenue shares.

Original main case specifies CU, one-month horizon, whole quantities, demand caps, two separate resources, rounded partial batches, all-cash no-inventory accounting and opening cash/equity. Fixed capacity services remain committed; no implicit cancellation saving is assumed.

Traditional actual-hour full allocation and practical-capacity ABC are distinguished. Every machine/setup/common cost reconciles to company expense, including unused capacity. Product-level resource assignments are never treated as automatically avoidable cash.

Main optimum has an independent analytic upper-bound certificate; equality proves unique global maximizer (80,28) even in the relaxation. Expanded setup-bound (80,44) has a separate upper-bound proof. The integer one-hour tie is retained, with no claim that a continuous marginal value always equals an integer increment.

Special-order idle and busy contexts have explicitly different available regular demand. Busy cost reoptimizes the complete regular plan after reserving both resources. External preparation/delivery 40 is separate from committed pools; no duplicate opportunity-cost charge.

Make/buy case is a separate next-month decision, not extra load on the main 300-hour budget. Avoidable batch cost, unchanged depreciation/common cost, additional buying inspection and released-capacity contribution are explicitly separated. Quote ceilings follow complete incremental scenarios.

Absorption/variable bridge fixes normal production capacity, rate, inventory conditions, no variances/write-downs and no payment lag. Both profit presentations reconcile to identical cash; only fixed manufacturing cost is deferred. No financial-reporting compliance rule or automatic overproduction recommendation is asserted.

Quality/contract admissibility, risk-neutral expected value, liquidity and external harm are distinguished. A positive private expected value does not establish compliance with the stipulated quality condition or positive social value.

All eight prompt/solution pairs were manually matched for inputs, units, endpoints, assumptions and requested explanations. Numerical tests support this prose audit rather than claiming to replace it.
